# Spring Cleaning Log

## Week One
I started on the wardrobe on a wet Saturday and pulled everything out onto the bed. Sorting took most of the afternoon: a keep pile, a mend pile, and a donate pile. In the end three bags went to the charity shop on the corner, mostly shirts I had not worn in two years and a pair of boots that never quite fitted. After that I turned to the basement shelves, which had become a dumping ground for paint tins and old cables. I emptied them one at a time, wiped each shelf down, and put back only what I could justify keeping. Two crates went to the tip and one box of tools moved to the shed.

## Week Two
The kitchen cupboards took a full morning. I pulled every jar out, checked dates, and found three bags of flour and a tin of anchovies from who knows when. Everything went back in groups: baking, spices, tins, and the everyday shelf I actually reach for. The hallway got repainted over the weekend, two coats of a soft off-white that makes the narrow space feel wider. Taping the edges was the slow part, and I still touched up around the doorframe on Sunday evening.

## Notes
I waited until the start of April for the windows, because the pollen is lighter then and the rain has mostly stopped. The whole flat smells fresher now. Next year I want to start in February so the job does not run into the good weather.
